sheets.name: actions-a
sheets.prompt: The ONLY character is the exact small pony shown in reference image 1; it is not a person. Create a clean transparent sprite sheet for a children's party game, 4 columns by 2 rows, eight separate full-body poses of that same pony. Preserve exact reference identity: a white quadruped pony with enormous flowing pastel pink, lavender, and cyan mane and tail, a small gold crown with three blue gems, very large blue eyes, and a yellow flower cutie mark. Four short pony legs and four hooves only; no hands, no fingers, no human anatomy, no wing, no unicorn horn. The mane and tail are cotton-candy colors. Bold dark navy outlines and smooth cel shading like reference. Use the reference as the strongest authority for character design. All figures face right, same head/torso scale, full mane and tail visible, generous transparent gutters. Ordered left to right, top row then bottom row: swim floating prone and paddling; balance wobble standing on three hooves with one foreleg raised, no platform; splat-throw playful forward toss gesture, empty hoof; wand-up rearing and lifting one empty hoof; broom-rise angled airborne ascent as though riding a separate broom, no broom drawn; broom-glide level forward flight, hooves tucked, no broom drawn; broom-zapped startled midair pose, no lightning or effects; count thoughtfully lifting a forehoof. Keep all art crisp, simple, and individually separated. Real alpha transparency. No backgrounds, glow, shadows, props, platforms, text, labels, borders, or other figures.

Four pony legs and hooves only, no hands or human anatomy, no wings or horn. No new crown, no extra accessory, no prop or other figure. True transparent background, no scene, floor, shadows, glow, motion lines, labels or text.

sheets.name: pose-twirl
sheets.prompt: Use the exact Cotton Candy pony from reference image 1: white pony, gold crown with blue gems, huge flowing cotton-candy pink/lavender/cyan mane and tail, large blue eyes, yellow flower cutie mark, clean dark navy outline and soft cel shading. Create one true-transparent horizontal strip with exactly four separate full-body views of the same pony, equal head/body size, crown and entire mane/tail visible in every cell, all four hooves grounded at a consistent baseline. This is a real 4-angle turning cycle, not a paper-thin spin: left to right (1) front view looking toward camera, (2) three-quarter view turned to her right, (3) full back view showing her mane, tail and flower mark, (4) three-quarter view returning toward front from the opposite side. Smooth naturally linked rotation while the body remains in place; no walk steps. Four pony legs and hooves only, no human arms/hands, no wings or horn. sheets.name: card-flip
sheets.prompt: Use reference image 1 as the exact Cotton Candy pony. Create one single isolated full-body sprite on a true transparent background: white quadruped pony, giant flowing pastel pink/lavender/cyan mane and tail, gold crown with blue gems, large blue eye, yellow flower cutie mark, bold navy outline and cel shading. Four pony legs and hooves only; no human arms or hands, no wings or horn. Pose for the party-game action “flip a memory card”: facing right in profile three-quarter view, neck curved downward and body leaning forward. Keep three hooves planted. The near-side front leg is unmistakably lifted and bent at the knee, reaching diagonally forward and down past the muzzle; its empty hoof is turned slightly downward as if tapping and turning a card on the ground. Leave a clear silhouette gap between the reaching hoof and planted legs. Her lowered muzzle and eye look directly at the same spot just ahead of that hoof. This must clearly read as reaching down to flip a memory card, absolutely not a somersault, tumble, roll, wave, or rear. Keep idle-sized head and body. Preserve full crown, mane, tail and all hooves without cropping. No card, table, platform, floor, shadows, props, scene, effects, text, labels or borders.
